text:
michael: PTAL — I pushed a follow-up addressing the two main nits and added a small rollback guard for the streaming path. Tests + unit added. CI link: https://ci.internal/1759
tara: thanks — quick question: does the rollback guard fire on partial responses too?
michael: yes, it only kicks in when the encoder fails to allocate > 2x the expected buffer. added comment and a tiny e2e to exercise partial streaming close. snippet:
```go
// if allocation unexpectedly spikes, revert to safe path
if alloc > expected*2 {
    log.Warn("alloc spike, switching to safe_stream")
    return safeStream(ctx, req)
}
```
jess: can you drop a note about the perf impact? want to know if we should enable this by default.
michael: perf hit is ~1% p99 increase in worst case (seen only in our synthetic stress test). added that to the PR description and linked benchmark: https://bench.internal/r/rc-1759
tara: CI running now. curious about merge timing — I'd like to avoid blocking tonight's canary window. if approved, can we queue for tomorrow morning?
michael: yep happy to hold merge until 09:00 PT tomorrow. also can squash if folks prefer smaller history.
jess: prefer keep history for this one (helps debug the guard later). small commits okay.
tara: +1 keep history. can you rebase off main to pick up the infra lint fix?
michael: rebased and force-pushed. CI passed: https://ci.internal/1759/build/42
ci-bot: Build passed — all checks green (unit, e2e, lint).
tara: LGTM — leaving merge to ops since we want the morning slot. tagging @merge-ops.
michael: thanks all :thumbsup:
